description: Two sound-but-lingering retro notes from fz-rh2.21: (1) Scheduler::rebased marks are only removed when the marked job next CONCLUDES; a job that never reruns keeps its mark forever (bounded by job count, no correctness impact — the mark only changes that job's own next conclude). (2) union_reads only ever grows a blocked job's subscription set; reads it no longer performs are dropped only at the next wait-free conclusion, so a long-blocked job can be woken by facts it stopped caring about (bounded wake amplification, no correctness impact). Neither blocks anything; address only with a holistic look at scheduler lifecycle — do not bolt on ad-hoc pruning.

comments.text:
INVESTIGATION (holistic look done; Outcome: no ad-hoc fix warranted now). scheduler.rs/deps.rs: Scheduler::rebased (HashSet<J>) and the union_reads read-subscription set are ALREADY cleared by the SAME event -- complete()'s wait-free (non-waiting) branch, back to back (scheduler.rs:268 rebased.remove; :274 replace_reads). They are one coherent lifecycle transition ('a settled conclusion replaces provisional state accumulated while blocked'), not two independent mechanisms needing unification. Both retro notes describe the identical residual case: a job that never reaches a wait-free conclude AGAIN (permanently blocked on a never-satisfied wait, or drive halts before it's popped). In that case there is no fresher state to reset TO -- the read-set and rebase mark are honest facts about the job's last ground-derived state.

A genuine holistic fix would require inventing JOB GARBAGE COLLECTION: jobs are immortal for the life of the World/Scheduler (facts.rs/deps.rs expose NO API to remove a job's reads/waits/outputs/subscriber entries; even function redefinition via stash_function_source leaves dead jobs inert, never reaped). Detecting an orphaned job (target fact retracted with no successor) and atomically tearing down all its scheduler state is a materially larger feature than this ticket, not a corollary.

BOUNDEDNESS confirmed by code (not just asserted): rebased is a HashSet -> re-insert is a no-op, size capped by distinct job count; union_reads capped by distinct FactUse the job can read (program size). Matches the ticket's own 'bounded by job count / bounded wake amplification' framing. No unbounded-growth path found.

RECOMMENDATION: close as documented/deferred to a future holistic scheduler-lifecycle (job-GC) pass. What would justify that pass: a MEASURED case where a long-lived World (multi-submission / editor-style incremental redefinition workload) accumulates enough dead-job cruft in rebased/reads/subscribers to show as real memory or wake-amplification cost. No such usage exists today (fz2 is single-shot run_cli). Until that signal exists, an ad-hoc prune is exactly the unjustified non-holistic patch this ticket and CLAUDE.md warn against.

title: Compiler2 fact-engine hygiene: prune rebased marks and shrink waiting subscriptions
